title: Porto Solutions — Implementation Kickoff & Runbook Walkthrough
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored runbook + network diagram (Jordan) by 2026-05-20
Porto to share non-prod sample payloads and traffic profile (Ethan) by 2026-05-22
Schedule a private-deploy tech deep dive with infra team (Alex + Porto infra) week of 2026-05-25
action_items: Jordan: Share Dedicated pricing tiers and burst policy doc (due 2026-05-20)
Alex: Prepare mini-benchmark plan (SLOs, perf tests) and baseline script (due 2026-05-24)
Sofia Hernandez: Provide encryption/KMS policy and required audit logs checklist (due 2026-05-21)
summary: Kickoff to align Porto Solutions and Redwood on implementation plan for production inference. Covered deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), initial runbook items, security requirements (KMS, SSO, audit logs), and a plan to run early benchmarks in non-prod. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. We'll do a quick roundtable and then jump into the runbook items.
00:15 Marcos (CTO): Hi — Marcos here, CTO at Porto. We have Lina, Ethan, Sofia, Tamika on call. We're excited to get this moving.
00:28 Jordan: Awesome. Quick agenda: introductions, goals for first 90 days, network/connectivity, security baseline, perf expectations, and next steps. Alex from our infra team will cover the tech bits.
00:40 Alex (SE): Hello all. I'll try to keep to the short version — we'll talk deploy modes, expected token throughput, and a proposed bench plan.
00:52 Lina (Head of Platform): We mostly care about predictable latency under 200ms p50 for chat flows, and controlling costs. Also strict data controls — some PII touches so we need to understand data residency.
01:10 Jordan: Understood. Can you give a quick snapshot of current stack? Where are you running inference today or is this greenfield?
01:22 Marcos: We're migrating from a mix — some on-prem inference runtimes and an internal API gateway. Primarily Kubernetes clusters in GCP for staging; production will be multi-cloud.
01:35 Ethan (SRE): For non-prod we can open up a peered VPC, but production needs to be more locked down — likely Private deployment in a VPC or Dedicated with strict network egress controls.
01:50 Sofia (Security): We need KMS integration, HSM option would be a plus, SAML SSO, and audit logs at token level. SOC2 is in flight so auditability is a must.
02:06 Alex: Great, those are common. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC peering and KMS/HSM integrations; audit logs and token-level tracing are available in the Console. There may be small naming mismatch in the console — the export labels sometimes say "request.id" or "session.id" in our older schema, Alex chuckles — we'll make sure mappings are clear.
02:30 Tamika (PM): Timeline — we want a pilot in non-prod within three weeks and go-to-prod within ten weeks if benchmarks look good. Is that realistic?
02:43 Jordan: That's tight but possible. We'll map milestones: week 1 network setup and access, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 pilot evaluation, weeks 4–10 rollouts and any security sign-offs.
03:01 Marcos: On sizing: our peak concurrent users for the chat use-case is ~120 qps, average message length 80 tokens, peak 300 token sequences. We'll share more exact profiles.
03:20 Alex: That works. For that footprint, initial Dedicated pool with autoscaling and burst capacity looks appropriate. We'll propose a config and cost sensitivity (batching vs latency tradeoffs).
03:35 Jordan: Quick caveat — batching improves cost but can increase tail latency. We recommend continuous batching with small max wait windows for chat.
03:45 Ethan: How does KV cache work with stateful chats? We maintain conversation caches on client side.
03:52 Alex: Redwood supports prefix/KV cache at runtime, we can surface details — slight transcription note: sometimes docs call it KV-cache and sometimes "context cache" — we'll consolidate. Cache reduces tokens and latency for repeated context.
04:07 Sofia: About encryption at rest and in transit — what's the default?
04:12 Alex: TLS in transit, encryption at rest by default. For customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS providers (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and HSM via partner flows. We'll capture the exact flow in the runbook.
04:28 Tamika: Any regulatory issues with data residency? Our legal requires EU data to stay in EU for some subproducts.
04:35 Jordan: We have region pinning — deployments can be pinned to specific regions and we can route EU traffic to an EU deployment. We'll document options and fallbacks.
04:50 Marcos: Great. Let's talk about non-prod access: we can open a CIDR to test infra, but production must be peering only.
04:58 Alex: Sounds fine; we'll provide VPC peering steps. Jordan: we'll send a diagram.
05:05 Jordan: Security checklist — Sofia do you have items off the top?
05:09 Sofia: SSO/SAML, role-based access (RBAC) mapping with our IdP, audit logs retention (we need 12 months), KMS, and a signed BAA for PHI — some customers touch healthcare data.
05:25 Jordan: Noted — BAA will be routed to legal. RBAC and SAML are supported; retention can be configured, longer retention may be an add-on.
05:38 Alex: On performance bench plan — propose 1) a baseline with sample payloads, 2) a soak test at 80% peak for 1 hour, 3) targeted p95/p99 latency runs. We'll use our benchmarking harness; Porto to provide payloads.
05:55 Ethan: We'll provide the payloads (anonymized) and an expected traffic replay script.
06:01 Alex: Perfect. We'll need a small non-prod account and an API key. For Private deploys we might do a short-lived dedicated node for benchmarking.
06:12 Tamika: Cost — how will we get cost visibility during pilot?
06:16 Jordan: Console has token-level cost breakdowns. For Dedicated we'll show per-pool cost and autoscale events; Optimize can give quant suggestions.
06:26 Marcos: About rollback and canary — we need a clear rollback plan if quality regresses.
06:31 Alex: Rollouts support canaries and automatic fallback to previous model or hosted variant. We'll include the canary thresholds in the runbook (e.g., quality/regression triggers).
06:45 Lina: Who will be our day-to-day contacts?
06:48 Jordan: Priya (CSM) will own onboarding and runbook coordination; Alex will own technical bench and infra; I'm the commercial lead. Priya: say hi.
06:57 Priya (CSM): Hi all — I'll own the kickoff checklist and coordinate meetings, and I'll also run adoption playbook items.
07:05 Marcos: Cool. Any special network requirements for Private?
07:10 Alex: For Private, we do either VPC peering or customer-managed VPN; port restrictions and egress rules are documented. Note: sometimes peering setup differs by cloud — e.g., GCP shared VPC naming or AWS account IDs — small manual steps.
07:28 Ethan: We use GCP shared VPC. Expect a couple of firewall rule quirks.
07:33 Alex: We'll attach a runbook page showing example commands and firewall rules.
07:40 Tamika: Can we get an ETA for the runbook doc?
07:43 Jordan: We'll send the first draft by 2026-05-20.
07:47 (silence / typing)
07:59 Sofia: On audit logs — token-level logs sound heavy. What's the data volume?
08:06 Alex: Good point — volume depends on retention and verbosity. We can sample events or roll up aggregates; full token-level retention for 12 months is possible but we'd discuss storage/add-on costs.
08:20 Marcos: Let's try a 30-day full retention in pilot, evaluate costs.
08:25 Jordan: Agreed.
08:28 Tamika: Any competitors or alternatives we should be aware of?
08:31 Marcos: We've looked at Anthropic for some generative tasks and also internal clusters at the moment.
08:36 Jordan: Noted. We'll share a short comparison matrix focusing on latency and cost.
08:42 Alex: Quick note about quantization — for some models quantized variants can reduce cost but may affect quality. We can recommend quantization profiles based on your eval set.
08:55 Tamika: Who will run evaluations? We'll have product own quality tests.
08:59 Alex: We can run joint evals — Redwood provides tooling and you provide ground truth. We'll set up a repo for that.
09:06 Ethan: On monitoring — what observability will we see?
09:09 Alex: Console shows per-route latency, model KPIs, token breakdowns, traces and error analysis. We'll provide tracing hooks for your APM.
09:19 Marcos: Any gotchas with multi-model routing? We want fallback to cheaper models during peak.
09:25 Alex: Smart routing can route by cost/latency and fall back to compatible variants; fallback config is part of the rollout policy.
09:33 Tamika: Ok, I'd like to see a suggested rollout cadence.
09:36 Jordan: We'll propose a canary over 10% traffic for 48 hours, expand to 50% for 72 hours, then full rollout if metrics stable, but we'll tailor to Porto's traffic patterns.
09:50 (brief crosstalk)
10:05 Priya: I'll schedule weekly check-ins for the next month — propose Tuesdays 9am PT.
10:11 Lina: Works for us.
10:14 Jordan: Anything else we missed?
10:18 Marcos: One more: data retention for logs associated with model prompts — legal wants prompt redaction options.
10:25 Alex: We support redaction flags and configurable redaction rules in the ingest path; we'll outline options.
10:33 Sofia: Also need proof of penetration testing schedule and SOC2 point-in-time report.
10:40 Jordan: We'll share our SOC2 attestation and pen-test cadence; legal will follow up on the BAA.
10:47 (pause)
10:55 Jordan: Quick recap: 1) Jordan sends runbook + network diagram by 5/20, 2) Porto shares payloads and traffic profile by 5/22, 3) Alex shares benchmark plan by 5/24, 4) schedule deep dive week of 5/25. Action owners captured.
11:12 Marcos: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
11:18 Priya: I'll send calendar invites for weekly cadence and a slot for the deep dive.
11:25 Tamika: Thanks — excited to get started.
11:30 End of recording.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional short mislabels; some product names may have been transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "KV cache" vs "context cache"). Links referenced: runbook template (internal link), network diagram (to be shared), benchmark harness repo (to be shared).
